To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the metal-bound alkene is the reactive species in a number of metal-directed alkene functionalizations; (2) the metal-bound alkenes are in general more reactive than the free ones; (3) the stereoelectronic effects of the metal-bound alkyl group in the metal-alkyl intermediates are important; (4) the stereochemical outcome of metal-alkyl reactions is determined by the relative stability of the two enantiomeric transition structures; (

metal-directed stereoselectivity in organic synthesis can be achieved by: (i) metal-assisted formation of a reactive intermediate (e.g., enolates, enols, enolates, carbenes, radicals), (ii) metal-assisted activation of an otherwise unreactive substrate (e.g., alkenes, alkynes) or (iii) metal-assisted delivery of a reactive species to a specific site on the substrate.

the stereoselectivity of a metal-directed alkene functionalization is determined by the nature of the metal, by the structure and the configuration of the substrate, and by the structure of the reagent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods of asymmetric synthesis based on the use of chiral auxiliaries and metal-directed stereoselectivity.
the development of new synthetic methodologies based on the stereoselective metal-mediated functionalization of aliphatic and alicyclic alkenes.
the development and application of novel stereoselective metal-mediated transformations in organic synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal is a key factor in the stereochemical course of the reactions of alkenes.
the metal is not only the "key", but also the "lock" for the stereoselective transformation of alkenes.
metal-directed reactions of alkenes are not only of great synthetic value but are also of great fundamental interest in understanding the mechanism of these reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metal-mediated reactions can be used to achieve high levels of stereocontrol in organic syntheses.
the metal is not only a "catalyst", but also a "directing group" for stereoselective alkene functionalizations.
metal-mediated or metal-catalyzed reactions can be used for stereoselective transformations of alkenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal-directed alkene functionalizations are highly stereoselective, and that the stereochemical outcomes are determined by the nature of the metal and the reaction conditions.
the metal-directed functionalizations are highly selective for the a-face of the alkene, and that the metal is the key to the a-face selectivity.
metal ions can be employed as chiral auxiliaries to direct the stereoselectivity of a variety of reactions of alkenes.
